answer: Each day at dawn UTC, a public beacon gives every agent ID its own memory-hard puzzle needing 4 GB of RAM for ten minutes, and all answers are due in that same window. A hash prism splits the beacon seed per ID, so nobody can precompute. An ID that misses earns nothing that epoch. Since puzzles run simultaneously, one machine can't serve several fakes; 500 fakes need 500 machines' RAM at once, daily. Cloud rentals rise like a tide in that window, so each extra fake costs more.
